description: A legal act that issues or wiki pages you can read refer to, as it is kept here: title, publisher, 'state' (fresh, stale, waiting — named and not read yet, or unreachable), 'asOf' — the day its text is as of, how many issues and pages refer to it ('references': total, and 'hidden' of them where you may not read), its articles with their offsets ('outline', on the first look) and a window of its text, at most 12000 characters. 'changedAt' is when its words were last found changed on the publisher's site, 'editions' the earlier texts kept (from, to — the days the site was asked, not the days the act was amended — and the headings each change was under), 'failing' a site that has stopped giving it. Pass 'find' («Article 18») to land on a place, or 'offset' to read on from 'nextOffset'. Reads no site: the text is the one already read. Name the act by the document id a reference gives, by its address, or by its key (e.g. 32015L0849); an act nothing you can read refers to is not found.

document.description: The act: a document id, its address, or its key (e.g. '32015L0849').

offset.description: Where to read from: a previous answer's nextOffset, or an outline entry's offset.
